title: An Open-Source Training Dataset for Foundation Models for Hyperparameter Optimization
claim: The dataset is a large, diverse collection whose composition spans many benchmark families, shown by task and search-space breakdowns.
layout: 2 donut charts plus legend table, left-to-right, nested outer ring
description: Two large donut charts sit side by side, followed by a legend table on the right. The left donut has "3,095 tasks" in its center and the right donut has "102 search spaces". Each ring is split into colored slices for benchmark families, with percentages labeled on the larger slices. A thin outer ring of tick segments marks the individual items inside each family. Colors match the legend: blue for TabRepo, red for HPO-B, green for FC-Net (masked), purple for NAS-201 (masked), orange for LC-Bench, gray for Global Opt., pink for PD1, teal for FC-Net, and magenta for NAS-201. The legend table lists task counts and search-space counts for each family. TabRepo dominates the left chart at 61%, while the right chart is more evenly spread. caption: Composition of our open-source dataset for pre-training foundation models for hyperparameter optimization. The dataset comprises $\statnumblackboxes$ tasks across $\statnumsearchspaces$ search spaces drawn from seven benchmarking families, including hyperparameter optimization, neural architecture search, and general black-box optimization benchmarks.
abstract: Most hyperparameter optimization methods require extensive tuning of their own hyperparameters, often limiting their ability to generalize across different benchmark families. Foundation models for hyperparameter optimization that learn optimization principles from a large collection of optimization trajectories offer a promising alternative, with the potential to outperform manually designed methods across diverse problem classes. However, prior work as either relied on non-public datasets or on purely synthetic data, limiting reproducibility and generalization to real-world problems. As a result, progress in this area has been constrained by the lack of large-scale, real-world, publicly available pre-training data. We introduce BBO-Pile, the first open-source dataset comprising over 500K optimization trajectories evaluated across 3,095 different hyperparameter optimization tasks and global optimization problems for different optimizers, which represents by far the largest public dataset for this task. Using this dataset, we train a family of foundation models at multiple scales, ranging from 2M to 80M parameters and from 200M to 2B training tokens, and study their scaling behavior with respect to compute. Our results demonstrate that large-scale pre-training is a viable and effective approach to imitate hyperparameter optimization methods, paving the way for future research in this direction.
